name: Rosewood Phnom Penh
positioning: City hotel in Cambodia's tallest skyscraper, with restaurants and lounges looking out over Phnom Penh
best_for: Food lovers who want Japanese, Chinese, French-Cambodian and steakhouse dining under one roof
Travelers interested in Cambodian contemporary art and Phnom Penh's 1960s architecture

facts.text: Zhan Liang serves Cantonese, Sichuanese and Northern Chinese dishes and has a tea library and a signature roasting station.
Brasserie Louis pairs views with French comfort food and Cambodian favorites made with local ingredients.
The Whisky Library is a cigar and whisky lounge offering rare single malts, 24 cigar varieties and skyline views.
Living Room is an all-day lounge for artisan coffee, cakes and evening drinks.
The hotel's curated art collection connects guests to the traditions of Cambodia.
Premier River Rooms have Tonle Sap views, custom art, a marble bath and a walk-in shower.
Mekong Suites have a king bed, a living room and views of the Mekong River.
The Norodom House has a grand foyer, a sitting room, a bedroom with a dressing chamber, a private study and a dining room.
Sense, A Rosewood Spa offers treatments inspired by traditional healing herbs and techniques.
A Khmer architectural tour explores Phnom Penh's 1960s heritage buildings aboard a traditional remork.
A self-guided tour through Phnom Penh's historic heart follows a quest for a lost Khmer antique and a mysterious French adventurer.

highlights.text: The hotel's restaurants and lounges have bird's-eye views from Cambodia's tallest skyscraper.
A hydroponic garden on Level 9 supplies all of the hotel's greens.
Sora received the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award 2025 for eco-mixology practices including zero-waste ingredients, local vermouth and in-house kombucha infusions.
CUTS is a steakhouse with hand-cut meats, a signature grill room, private suites and a wine cellar with over 3,000 bottles.
Iza brings the spirit of a Japanese izakaya, with a robata-yaki grill, sushi counter, noodle corner and a curated selection of sake.

considerations.text: The hotel's restaurants and lounges sit high up in Cambodia's tallest skyscraper, so this is a high-rise city stay.
WhataHotel notes a modern high-rise setting rather than traditional Cambodian architecture.
